# Task: Add Currency Field Conversion to Metabase Query Export

## Background

We need to add currency field conversion functionality to Metabase's query result export module, allowing automatic currency formatting based on site settings.

## Files to Create/Modify

- `src/metabase/query_processor/middleware/currency_formatter.clj` (new)
- `src/metabase/api/dataset.clj` (modify export paths)
- `test/metabase/query_processor/middleware/currency_formatter_test.clj` (new)

## Requirements

### Currency Formatter Middleware

- Read site-currency setting from `src/metabase/models/setting.clj`
- Format columns with type `:type/Currency`
- Apply conversion to result set

### Integration Points

- Call middleware in `POST /api/dataset/csv` export path
- Call middleware in `POST /api/dataset/json` export path

### Conversion Logic

- Support common currency pairs (USD, EUR, CNY, etc.)
- Handle null values gracefully
- Non-currency columns should not be affected

### Expected Functionality

- Currency conversions work correctly (e.g., USD → CNY with proper exchange rate)
- Null values are skipped without raising errors
- Non-currency columns remain unchanged
- Invalid currency configuration falls back to default behavior

## Acceptance Criteria

- Implementation compiles and runs without errors
- All currency conversion scenarios work as specified
- Edge cases are handled appropriately

execution_gaps.local_state: Task requires modifying `src/metabase/api/dataset.clj` to call middleware in POST /api/dataset/csv and POST /api/dataset/json export paths
execution_gaps.agent_action: Agent never read, modified, or even located `src/metabase/api/dataset.clj`; instead integrated the middleware globally in `postprocess.clj`
execution_gaps.observed_problem: The task explicitly listed `src/metabase/api/dataset.clj` as a file to modify and specified integration at the CSV and JSON export API paths specifically. The agent did not modify this file at all, and placed the middleware in the general post-processing pipeline instead of the specific export paths.

trajectory_evidence.description: Agent searched for dataset.clj but found nothing at the expected path
Bash search for dataset.clj returned no output, meaning the file was not found
Agent searched api/ directory for dataset files but found nothing
Second dataset search returned no output
Agent integrated middleware into postprocess.clj middleware list globally, not in dataset export API endpoints
Git status shows only postprocess.clj and system/settings.clj modified, no dataset.clj changes

execution_gaps.local_state: Task requires implementing actual currency conversion logic (e.g., USD to CNY with proper exchange rate)
execution_gaps.agent_action: Agent created a `format-currency-value` function that is a complete no-op stub returning the value unchanged, with no exchange rate conversion implemented
execution_gaps.observed_problem: The acceptance criteria states 'Currency conversions work correctly (e.g., USD → CNY with proper exchange rate)'. The `format-currency-value` function ignores its `_currency` parameter and simply returns `value` unchanged, meaning no actual conversion takes place.

trajectory_evidence.description: Agent wrote format-currency-value as a stub: '[value _currency] value' with a comment 'returns the value as-is'
Final file content shows format-currency-value still returns value unchanged with no conversion logic

execution_gaps.local_state: The test for null values checks that the second (non-null) row's price field is null
execution_gaps.agent_action: Agent wrote a test asserting `(nil? (nth (last @rows) 1))` where `last @rows` would be `[2 150.00]`, meaning it checks whether 150.00 is nil
execution_gaps.observed_problem: The test assertion at the end of `test-currency-formatter-with-null-values` is logically wrong: it checks the last row (which has value 150.00) for being nil, rather than checking the first row (which has nil). This test would fail when run.

trajectory_evidence.description: Agent wrote test with rows [1 nil] and [2 150.00], then asserted (nil? (nth (last @rows) 1)) where last @rows is [2 150.00]

execution_gaps.local_state: Task requires reading site-currency setting from `src/metabase/models/setting.clj`
execution_gaps.agent_action: Agent added the `site-currency` defsetting to `src/metabase/system/settings.clj` instead of `src/metabase/models/setting.clj` as specified
execution_gaps.observed_problem: The task description explicitly says to 'Read site-currency setting from `src/metabase/models/setting.clj`'. The agent placed the new defsetting in a different file (`system/settings.clj`) and there is no `src/metabase/models/setting.clj` matching that path.

trajectory_evidence.description: Agent found the actual setting file at `src/metabase/settings/models/setting.clj` not `src/metabase/models/setting.clj`
Agent added site-currency defsetting to system/settings.clj, not to any models/setting.clj
Final verification shows site-currency in system/settings.clj

27: ### Data summary
28: 
29: Data summary gives you a quick snapshot of the transform's input and output tables:
30: 
31: - **Input and output tables**: table name, row count, column count.
32: - **Field-level stats**: data type, distinct count, nil percentage (number of null values), range, and averages.
33: 
34: ### Column distributions
35: 
36: The Column distributions lens visualizes how data distributions change through the transform. This lens can help you spot unexpected filtering or aggregation effects. This lens is only available when columns match between input and output tables (so you may not see it for transforms that aggregate data).
37: 
38: The Column distributions lens can be slow on large datasets because it computes distribution stats for every matched column.

125: ## I added fields to my database but don't see them in Metabase
126: 
127: Metabase may not sync all of your fields. Since any document in a MongoDB collection can contain any number of fields, the only way to get 100% coverage of all fields would be to scan every single document in every single collection. The reason Metabase doesn't do a full scan is because it would put too much strain on your database.
128: 
129: Instead, Metabase gets a sample of the fields in a collection by scanning a sample of 1000 documents in each collection (the first 500 documents and the last 500 documents in each collection).
130: 
131: If you're not seeing all of the fields show up for a collection in Metabase, one workaround is to include all possible keys in the first document of the collection, and give those keys null values. That way, Metabase will be able to recognize the correct schema for the entire collection.

137: ## Database routing
138: 
139: With database routing, an admin can build a question once using one database, and the question will run its query against a different database with the same schema depending on who is viewing the question.
